title: Kumzari language - Wikipedia
text: Kumzari is a Southwestern Iranian language that has similarities with Persian, Luri, Achomi and Balochi languages. Although vulnerable, it survives today with between 4,000 and 5,000 speakers.

title: Kumzari | Ethnologue Free
text: Kumzari is an endangered indigenous language of Oman and Iran. It belongs to the Indo-European language family. Direct evidence is lacking, but the language is thought to be used as a first language by a decreasing number of young people.

title: Kumzari | ResearchGate
text: Kumzari is an endangered language spoken by about 4000 people in Oman, the United Arab Emirates and Iran. Speakers of the main dialect are found on the Musandam Peninsula of Oman and in small groups in cities along the Gulf coast of the United Arab Emirates.
